function_v0.doc:
Emit one canary packet.

`max_fee` is a hard ceiling in stroops. Passing 0 disables the check, which
is deliberately not the default in the runner: an unattended hourly job with
no ceiling is an unbounded standing authorisation against the submitter.

FEE MECHANICS \xe2\x80\x94 the thing that is not in any Stellar OApp doc.
`EndpointV2::send` does NOT pull the fee from the sender. `pay_messaging_fees`
reads `native_token.balance(<endpoint>)` \xe2\x80\x94 the ENDPOINT's own balance \xe2\x80\x94 and
pays each worker out of it, refunding whatever is left to `refund_address`.
So the OApp must PUSH the fee to the endpoint *before* calling `send`;
holding the balance itself yields `EndpointError::InsufficientNativeFee` (#6)
no matter how rich the OApp is. The endpoint's own source says it in one line
and nowhere else: "OApp sender needs to transfer the fees to the endpoint
before sending the message".

The transfer is a direct call from this contract to the native SAC, so
`from.require_auth()` inside the token is satisfied by the direct-invo
function_v0.name: ping

function_v0.doc: Quote a loopback packet without sending. Used by the runner to enforce a\nspend ceiling before committing, so a price-feed excursion cannot silently\ndrain the submitter.
function_v0.name: quote

function_v0.doc:
Configure this OApp's own security stack on the endpoint.

This exists because an OApp that cannot configure itself is unusable on
Stellar. The default send/receive configs point at DVNs with no `dst_config`
(and on mainnet, at the zero-address "Dead DVN"), so every OApp MUST set a
custom config \xe2\x80\x94 and `endpoint.set_config(caller, oapp, ...)` requires
`caller` to be authorised for `oapp`.

Passing the contract itself as BOTH `caller` and `oapp` sidesteps the
delegate mechanism entirely: a contract is inherently authorised over its
own configuration, so no `set_delegate` round trip is needed. The admin
gate here is what stops anyone else driving it.

`config_type`: 2 = CONFIG_TYPE_SEND_ULN, 3 = CONFIG_TYPE_RECEIVE_ULN.
function_v0.name: configure

function_v0.doc: Receiving side. A loopback packet is never executed \xe2\x80\x94 we need `packet_sent`\nand the resulting attestation, not delivery \xe2\x80\x94 so this exists only so the\ncontract presents a complete OApp surface if anything ever does deliver.
function_v0.name: lz_receive

udt_struct_v0.doc: Endpoint `set_config` parameter. Fields are already alphabetical, which is the\norder `#[contracttype]` emits regardless of declaration order.

udt_struct_v0.doc:
Mirrors the deployed EndpointV2 ABI. `#[contracttype]` sorts fields
alphabetically at codegen, and the endpoint's own declaration is already in
alphabetical order, so the XDR maps match. Reordering these breaks the call
silently \xe2\x80\x94 the map keys, not the positions, are what bind.
